description: The plot illustrates how classification accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from 0 to about 3000, with major tick labels shown at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging from 60 to 85 with regularly spaced tick labels every 5 units (60, 65, 70, 75, 80, 85). The Base line is black with circular markers and a solid line, increasing from about 61 at the leftmost point to about 67 at the rightmost point, with intermediate points near 63.5 and 65. The FT line is blue with downward triangle markers and a solid line, rising from about 62.5 to about 68.5, passing through roughly 65 and 67.8. The IKE line is red with upward triangle markers and a solid line, increasing from about 64.5 to about 70.2, with midpoints around 67.8 and 69.4. The MEND line is brown with diamond markers and a solid line, moving upward from about 66 to about 74, with points near 71.3 and 73.5. The MEMIT line is purple with pentagon markers and a solid line, increasing from about 66.5 to about 72.7, with intermediate values around 70.2 and 71.4. The ROME line is green with square markers and a solid line, starting around 72.3 and increasing to about 77.7 by the rightmost point, with intermediate points near 76.0 and 77.6.
